summary: Differentiate sampled values with respect to cumulative polyline arclength.

capability: Differentiate sampled values with respect to cumulative polyline chord arclength.
operation: ordered planar vertices and matched values -> endpoint-inclusive derivative in value per length
discovery.model: Direct three-point unequal-spacing finite differences, with one-sided quadratic stencils at both endpoints.
discovery.geometry: Ordered planar polyline; vertices and values are one-dimensional and matched. No smooth-curve arclength or periodic closure is reconstructed.
discovery.boundary: Endpoints use one-sided stencils; N>=3, finite matched inputs and distinct adjacent vertices are required, while periodic closure and noise statistics are excluded.

identity.direction: ordered vertices and values to endpoint-inclusive derivative
identity.definition: Use a three-point unequal-spacing stencil at interior and one-sided quadratic stencils at both endpoints.
identity.model: Direct finite-difference derivative on cumulative adjacent-vertex distance.
identity.coordinates: Vertices in length units; values in caller units.
identity.boundary: No periodic closure is inferred; endpoints use one-sided stencils.
assumptions: Vertices and values are finite, matched, and have N>=3.
The derivative follows caller vertex order.

preconditions: Vertices and values are finite, matched, and have N>=3.
supported: Nonuniform spacing and manufactured polynomial cases in the listed tests.
excluded: Smooth-curve arclength reconstruction, periodic endpoint stencils, and noise statistics.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for wrong shapes, too few samples, nonfinite values, or duplicate adjacent vertices.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the derivative is direct.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No derivative array is returned after validation failure.

example.description: Differentiate x^2 on a nonuniform three-point polyline.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.fieldline import d_ds_arclength
p=np.array([[0.,0.],[.3,0.],[1.,0.]])
assert np.allclose(d_ds_arclength(p,p[:,0]**2),2*p[:,0])
example.expected: The returned derivative is [0,0.6,2] within the assertion tolerance.

scope: Only the explicitly stated finite input domain and direct-test fixtures
verification.evidence_ceiling: Numerical evidence for the named fixtures only; it does not establish arbitrary-input correctness or experimental physical validation.
known_limitations: Polyline chord lengths are used; no true smooth-curve arclength is inferred
Periodic endpoint stencil and noise statistics are unqualified
